stories.title: Bilawal says KP governor's rule could end if opposition agrees to fight against terrorism
summary: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Sunday that if the opposition was willing to fight against terrorism and “we agree on a plan”, governor’s rule and emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could end.

He added that the country had now once again reached the point where “some forces want to take down Pakistan’s flag in Swat” and there was a fight against terrorism ongoing across the entire country, while security forces, law enforcers and the public were being targeted.
For this reason, he said, the PPP had highlighted the need for a new NAP and consensus on the fight against terrorism, while also extending an invitation to the opposition to play a part in this.

stories.title: 8 India-sponsored terrorists killed in Quetta, Khuzdar, Nushki districts: ISPR
summary: Security forces have killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during three intelligence-based operations conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
Separately, during a sanitisation operation in Nushki district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and “after an intense fire exchange, two India-sponsored terrorists were sent to hell”.
On the night of Oct 12/13, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and killed five terrorists during an IBO in Washuk, ISPR said.

stories.title: Tensions over headscarves, Israel test Azerbaijan-Turkiye ties
summary: The normally close ties between Turkiye and Azerbaijan have come under strain, fuelled by a dispute over Baku’s restrictions on headscarves in schools and disagreements over Israel.

But it also highlighted tensions over the growing rapprochement between Azerbaijan and Israel since Baku’s 2020 Karabakh war with arch-foe Armenia, when the Israelis supplied them with drones and other weaponry.

Turkiye’s ties with Israel, by contrast, could hardly be worse, with Erdogan accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza and Ankara regularly releasing images of top-level talks with the leaders of Hamas, whose October 2023 attacks on Israel sparked the latter’s onslaught on Gaza.

stories.title: ‘The joke is on us’
summary: For over a month, young people camped at Jantar Mantar – Delhi’s iconic protest site.
In India, young reporters and small digital outlets have covered the protests that big channels ignored.

What is happening in Delhi is less a story about India than a story about the region, about governments that have learned to switch off the internet faster than they can create jobs, and young people who have learned to make jokes faster than governments can ban them.

stories.title: Salman Ali Agha hits ton but Sri Lanka’s Malinga restricts Pakistan to 305 in ODI tri-series opener
summary: Salman Ali Agha celebrated his return to the Pakistan side after his unceremonious axing from the Test team two months ago with his third One-day International century in the tri-series opener against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday.
Pakistan were 279-6 when Salman departed in the 47th over, mistiming a lofted shot off Fernando to Dasun Shanaka at long-on.
Pakistan were bowled out for 305 in 49.5 overs, with Malinga’s incisive spell ensuring Sri Lanka finished the innings strongly after Salman had threatened to take the total well beyond 320.

stories.title: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen
summary: Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said two officers were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the rebel group claimed it shot the aircraft down.
The incident comes a week after strikes by the Houthis killed 13 people at Riyadh’s international airport, the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
Pakistan, which has signed two defence agreements with Riyadh, has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Maldives President Muizzu to visit Pakistan from Oct 20-22: FO
summary: Maldives’ President Dr Mohamed Muizzu will undertake a three-day state visit to Pakistan from Oct 20-22 at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Sunday.
The forthcoming visit reflected the “shared commitment of both countries to further strengthening their bilateral partnership and opening new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, it added.
In 2015, former Maldivian president Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom undertook a two-day state visit to Pakistan on May 6-7 at the invitation of then-premier Nawaz Sharif.

stories.title: My father survived the Karsaz bombing; each new terror attack takes us back there
summary: My father had found his way to an ambulance that was taking him to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre — a designated hospital for injuries and casualties — but he eventually ended up at (what is now known as) the Dr Ruth Pfau Civil Hospital Karachi.
Had any patient in his condition come to the hospital that night, they would have been surgically operated on by my father and his team.
Some among us are still able to deal with terrorism using the standard emotional survival process mentioned at the beginning of this piece.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz inaugurates Daanish School in Islamabad, stresses equal academic opportunities
summary: Daanish schools, originally introduced by the Punjab government, aim to provide quality education to marginalised and talented students.
Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui also spoke on the occasion.
In March, thousands of students across Pakistan sought admission to the school, which received over 7,000 applications against just 210 seats.

stories.title: First Pakistani astronaut to undertake space mission from China on Nov 25: Ahsan Iqbal
summary: Pakistan’s first astronaut will undertake a space mission from a Chinese space centre on November 25, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said on Sunday.

The minister made the announcement while addressing the concluding ceremony of World Space Week in Narowal, held in collaboration with the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco), the planning ministry said in a statement.

According to the handout, the planning minister also said the country was aiming to achieve a lunar landing by 2035, expressing hope that Pakistan’s cooperation with China would help it “reach new heights in space exploration”.

stories.title: Musk back in the spotlight, but politics dims the awe
summary: Now Musk is back in Trump’s good graces, after a spectacular falling-out that followed his exit from DOGE in May 2025.
Last week, Trump presented Musk with the nation’s top science medal, calling him a “national treasure” and “our modern-day Thomas Edison”.
The same may be true of Musk’s dealings with Washington.

stories.title: What is holding up the US-India trade deal?
summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to visit India for the second time this year, as Washington seeks to bolster ties with a strategic partner despite months of friction over a trade deal.

India and the United States agreed in February on the framework for an interim deal under which Washington would lower reciprocal tariffs from 25 per cent to 18pc and India would reduce duties on a range of industrial and agricultural goods.

India is also wary of new trade measures by Washington that could impact it, including an investigation into alleged unfair practices in several countries and a new law that allows for up to 100pc tariffs on nations that purchase Russian oil.

stories.title: Pakistan suspends Iran trade corridors over 'security, smuggling concerns'
summary: GWADAR/QUETTA: Pakistan has suspended trade with Iran through the official Gabd-Rimdan (250) and Taftan border crossings, it emerged on Saturday.

Shahid Rind, adviser to the Balochistan chief minister on media and political affairs, said the “purpose of the temporary closure of the Pak-Iran border is to address security concerns, prevent smuggling, and make the border system more effective”.
The visit came a couple of months after it was reported that trade between Pakistan and Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing had come to a complete halt.

stories.title: Four sentenced to death in Lahore in 2022 blasphemy case
summary: LAHORE: A sessions court on Saturday sentenced four men to death in a 2022 blasphemy case registered by the then cybercrime wing of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA).
Each convict was sentenced to death and fined Rs500,000 under Section 295-C of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), and given life imprisonment under Section 295-B.
The death sentences are subject to confirmation by the Lahore High Court, to which a reference will be sent.

stories.title: Digging in Karachi for Red Line damages gas pipeline, disrupts supply
summary: The disruption affected Gulshan-i-Iqbal, areas around Mazar-i-Quaid, parts of Garden, Saddar, Burns Road and several other localities.

A spokesperson for the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) said that the high-pressure pipeline near the Gulshan-i-Iqbal telephone exchange on University Road was damaged at around 1pm during BRT construction activity.

Several households reported disruption in preparing afternoon meals, while commercial eateries and roadside hotels in Saddar and Garden saw a rush of customers as many people had no option but to dine out or take food home for their families.

stories.title: KP education dept orders safety audit of school buildings
summary: Meanwhile, the Peshawar district administration has launched inspections of public and private educational institutions and seminaries to assess building safety and improve the learning environment.

Also, the Lower Dir district administration has launched a security audit of government and private school buildings to assess their structural integrity, physical condition and suitability for educational activities.

Assistant commissioner (headquarters) Adnan Mumtaz Khattak and members of the inspection committee visited several government and private schools in Swabi tehsil to review the condition of their buildings and security arrangements.

stories.title: Ram Leela Temple in Dera Ismail Khan sealed amid demolition fears
summary: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: The authorities here on Saturday locked and sealed the historic Ram Leela Temple in Rahim Bazaar days after civil society activists intervened to stop the demolition of the heritage building for the construction of a commercial plaza at the site.
The latest development came as civil society representatives and members of the Hindu community held a joint meeting to discuss the reported move to demolish the temple.

They expressed concern over any move to demolish the temple and said civil society, the business community, writers and heritage advocates would resist any action that could damage the city’s historical heritage.

stories.title: Japan to launch historic round-trip mission to Mars moon
summary: Japanese scientists are preparing a mission to Mars’s moons to retrieve samples that could help unlock the origins of the solar system and life on Earth, in what aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region.

One of the differences between JAXA’s past asteroid probes and the MMX mission is that this time “we have to travel very close to Mars and return”, which means escaping the planet’s heavy gravity, Kawakatsu told reporters.
China’s mission US and Chinese space agencies have been racing to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth.

stories.title: One in three adults in Pakistan lives with psychological disorder: study
summary: KARACHI: Pakistan’s first nationally representative mental health survey has shown that nearly one in three adults is living with a diagnosable mental and behavioural disorder, highlighting a major public health challenge affecting millions of people across the country.

Experts term findings of first national mental health survey ‘most reliable’ Nearly 18,000 adults from all four provinces participated in the 2018-2022 study, providing the first nationally representative picture of mental health in the country.

Prof Anjum Memon, Chair in Epidemiology and Public Health Medicine at Brighton and Sussex Medical School (UK) and the senior co-author of the study, said: “This is a landmark moment for mental health research in Pakistan.

stories.title: 'Serious incident' at Canada base causes deaths, sparks fire: govt
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney had posted to X earlier on Saturday that “a serious incident creating a major fire” had occurred at the base.

Neither offered details on the number of casualties or the nature of the incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, located about 200 kilometres southeast of Edmonton. “We will have more to say in the coming hours and days,” McGuinty said.
Alberta’s office responsible for overseeing provincial elections said the advance voting station in Wainwright had closed.

stories.title: Out-of-control truck kills 13 at religious festival in India's Madhya Pradesh
summary: A speeding truck in India killed 13 people when it ploughed into a crowd at a Hindu festival, officials said on Sunday, with President Droupadi Murmu describing the deaths as “heartbreaking”.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency cited hospital officials as saying 13 people had died. “I express my deepest condolences to the bereaved families and pray for the swift recovery of those injured,” Murmu said on social media.

The incident comes a day after at least 17 people were killed and two dozen more injured on Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that was likely caused by sudden rainfall during a Hindu religious gathering, officials said.

stories.title: Pakistan juniors crush Canada at Johor Cup
summary: Pakistan junior hockey team continued their impressive run in the Sultan of Johor Cup 2026, defeating Canada 6-2 in their second match to record back-to-back victories.
Pakistan restored their three-goal advantage in the 38th minute when Rana Waleed scored the team's fourth goal.
Canada, Pakistan, China, Malaysia and Japan compete in the competitions.

stories.title: Visa delay costs Waseem five-fight deal
summary: Pakistan’s professional boxer Mohammad Waseem, the WBA bantamweight gold champion, on Sunday said a delay in obtaining a Schengen visa cost him a potential five-fight deal with a Mexican promotion company.
Waseem is a rare fighter who won the WBC World silver flyweight title in only his fourth professional bout.

Waseem has lost only two fights in his professional career, both of them world title bouts against South Africa's Moruti Mthalane and England's Sunny Edwards, despite the Pakistani boxer putting up strong performances in both contests.

stories.title: Rizwan set for domestic cricket return
summary: Sources said Rizwan has been allowed by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to feature in domestic cricket.
Rizwan, who has been facing an investigation by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), was initially not permitted to play first-class cricket, alongside fellow batsman Imam-ul-Haq.
Rizwan subsequently challenged the proceedings in the Lahore High Court (LHC), which dismissed his petition and advised him to cooperate with the NCCIA.

stories.title: Smith says head blow left him anxious in first test concussion scare
summary: Australia batsman Steve Smith said he was anxious after being hit on the head and facing the prospect of another concussion after a blow playing against South Africa in the first test a week ago.
PASSED CONCUSSION PROTOCOLS But then Smith did not take to the field at the start ‌of South ⁠Africa's second innings on Monday, instead being subjected to the concussion protocols, which he passed.

He also suffered a concussion after being hit on the head in practice during Australia's One Day International series ⁠in England in 2020 and two months later, back home in Sydney, woke on the morning of the second ODI against India with vertigo and was sick.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz stresses equal opportunities in education to realize Quaid's vision
summary: Recalling the initiative’s origins during his tenure as Punjab chief minister, PM Shehbaz questioned why children from affluent families could attend elite institutions while millions of equally talented children from poor households could not access comparable education.
The prime minister said the achievements of Daanish School graduates showed what children could accomplish when given access to education.
The Daanish Schools initiative was launched in Punjab in 2010 under then chief minister Shehbaz Sharif to provide quality education to talented children from underprivileged backgrounds.

stories.title: Trump paused Russia sanctions to 'analyse' impact on global economy: Rubio
summary: Trump’s executive order came after he struck a deal with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin to allow exports of Russian diesel in exchange for the easing of sanctions.

Polls show Trump’s Republicans are likely to receive a drubbing at the polls. “The diesel that Putin was going to sell, they were (going to) make it available to the global market one way or the other.
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said he feared the United States would lift more sanctions on Russia and that Trump’s action “rewards” Putin.

stories.title: Five K-dramas that couldn’t stick the landing
summary: Starring Yoo Yeon-seok and Chae Soo-bin, the series follows Baek Sa-eon and Hong Hee-joo, a couple whose relationship has been defined by emotional distance and years of silence.
As the story progresses, increasingly dramatic developments compete with the central relationship, and the search for a missing spouse eventually takes the drama into a war-zone setting.

Dynamite Kiss (2025) Photo: The Drama Corner A chance encounter, an unforgettable kiss and a workplace romance provide the foundation for Dynamite Kiss, a series that initially embraces the lighter side of Korean romantic comedy.

stories.title: 12 killed as truck runs over devotees near temple in central India: police
summary: At least 12 people were killed and dozens of others injured when a truck hit devotees near a temple in India's central Madhya Pradesh state, a police official said early Sunday.

The accident occurred in Gwalior when a truck loaded with paddy lost control on a steep road and crashed into the outer wall and gate of the Sheetla Mata Temple, senior police official Dharmveer Singh said.
A day earlier, at least 17 people were killed and several others injured in a stampede at a religious festival in north Kolkata in India, NDTV reported.

stories.title: FM Dar, Iranian FM discuss regional situation, OIC meeting in Baghdad
summary: In a post on X, the FO said the two leaders also discussed the next meeting of the R-4 grouping, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, during a telephone conversation. “The two leaders exchanged views on recent regional developments," the ministry added.
Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, under the R-4 framework, condemned the attacks and backed the kingdom’s right to take legitimate measures to counter the threat.

The Istanbul meeting, however, assumes added significance because it will be the first major R-4 engagement since Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7.

stories.title: Imran Khan challenges 'unconstitutional' exit notice in Bombay High Court
summary: Indian actor Imran Khan challenged a notice directing him to leave India by October 28, arguing that the order was unconstitutional and that authorities failed to properly consider his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status.

According to Gulf News, the 44-year-old actor filed a writ petition in the Bombay High Court on Saturday against the Leave India Notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) on October 14.
The FRRO also issued a show-cause notice asking the actor to explain why his OCI registration should not be cancelled under Section 7D(e) of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

stories.title: US vice president says he has yet to decide on 2028 presidential run
summary: United States Vice President JD Vance said he has not decided whether to run for president in 2028, acknowledging he could ultimately opt out despite being widely viewed as a leading contender to succeed President Donald Trump.

Read: Vance suggests disagreement with Trump over Iran war Vance also defended the administration's economic and foreign policies, blaming former President Joe Biden's administration for neglecting manufacturing while acknowledging that reversing its decline would take time.

stories.title: Maldivian president to visit Pakistan on Oct 20-22 as ties mark 60 years: FO
summary: Muizzu will visit Pakistan at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, accompanied by First Lady Sajidha Mohamed and a high-level delegation comprising cabinet ministers and senior officials, according to the statement.

Read: CDF Munir, Maldives parliament speaker discuss bilateral cooperation and regional security “They will also exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest,” it added.

The visit will also feature a Pakistan–Maldives Business Forum, "aimed at promoting greater interaction between the business communities of the two countries and exploring new opportunities for trade and investment,” the statement read.

stories.title: Broken record: Contested boundaries, founding challenges and a provincial govt dismissed
summary: In more welcome news, the bureaucracy in the nascent state rolled up their sleeves to take up the task of nation-building — which remains a work in progress, mind you — while congratulations continued to pour in welcoming Pakistan to the comity of nations.
Aug 19 was the first working day of the Pakistan government.

Meanwhile, as the Aug 18 issue reported, Pakistan submitted its application to the United Nations. “The formal letter of application arrived from Karachi at United Nations Headquarters today [Aug 16].

stories.title: California governor says US military aid to Israel must be conditioned
summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom said Saturday that United States military aid to Israel "has to be conditioned," describing the position as increasingly becoming the Democratic Party's consensus as he campaigns in New Hampshire ahead of a potential 2028 presidential run.

"Aid has to be conditioned," Newsom told the Washington Examiner, citing settler violence in the occupied West Bank and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies, which he said undermine prospects for a two-state solution.
Newsom has previously criticised Netanyahu while expressing support for Israel, including visiting the country in 2023 to meet survivors of the Hamas attack.

stories.title: Judicial probe sought into Hina Javed’s murder
summary: RAWALPINDI: The family of Hina Javed, a married woman murdered in Rawalpindi two months ago, has demanded that the prime minister and the chief minister of Punjab form a special judicial commission to ensure a transparent investigation into the case.
They also requested that the DNA and forensic reports be shared with the family.
Speaking at a press conference at the National Press Club in Islamabad, the victim’s brother, Fahad Javed, stated that the brutality with which Hina Javed was murdered was beyond description.

stories.title: Construction of underpass in front of Rawalpindi's Armed Forces Institute of Cardiology begins
summary: A senior official of the district administration told Dawn that the proposal had been sent to the government to start work on the underpass to cater to the traffic rush on the main square commonly known as Station Mor in front of AFIC.
He said Nespak had also sent a report to the government stating that it was necessary to construct the underpass to make The Mall and Peshawar Road signal free from Koral Chowk to Motorway Chowk.

He said the National Highway Authority was already working to expand the road from Chungi No 26 towards Motorway Chowk with the Punjab Highway Department working on the two underpasses to make a signal-free corridor from Ammar Chowk to Motorway Chowk.

stories.title: Teenage girl, woman shot dead in Lakki Marwat in separate incidents
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: A teenage girl was shot dead inside her house in the Khankhel Mandozai area of Lakki Marwat district, police said on Friday.
The body was shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital for postmortem examination, while a case was registered against the suspects under relevant sections of the law at Bargai police station.

Jehangir Khan, 79, father of the deceased woman, told Bargai police that his son-in-law, Gul Nawar Khan, was abroad and his daughter had been living in a rented house in the Kotka Amin area of Sra Darga.

stories.title: Pakistan to launch first astronaut into space from China on Nov 25: Ahsan Iqbal
summary: Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal announced on Sunday that Pakistan’s first astronaut would embark on a space mission from China on November 25, as he set out the country’s ambitions for a lunar mission by 2035, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.
He also announced plans to establish Pakistan’s first Space Museum at the University of Narowal to promote scientific awareness and encourage young people to pursue space science and technology.
The mission is part of wider cooperation between Pakistan and China in space science and technology.

stories.title: Restoration of peace first priority: KP governor
summary: Earlier, he told the convocation that providing quality healthcare, resolving doctors’ genuine concerns and improving the health service delivery system were among the advisory council’s top priorities, according to a statement issued by his office.
The governor said that the council would focus on providing modern medical facilities, improving healthcare infrastructure and establishing better hospitals in underserved and remote areas.
The governor stressed that effective coordination among doctors, medical institutions, organisations and the advisory council was essential to improving healthcare delivery.
